The turbine had a chord-to-radius ratio of 0.49 and a preset pitch angle of -6 degrees.
The chord length of the blades was 4.06 cm, the span was 23.4 cm, and the turbine radius to the quarter chord was 8.23 cm.
The Reynolds number based on chord and freestream was 44,000.
The turbine blockage ratio was 9.3% and the solidity was 0.16 for the two-bladed configuration.
The virtual camber was consistently positive throughout the cycle, with the greatest variations at low tip-speed ratios.
The virtual incidence followed a similar trend to the virtual camber, maintaining a positive value that increased the upstream angle of attack.
The negatively cambered blades slightly improved the symmetrical blade performance by enhancing downstream flow reattachment.
The positively cambered blades exhibited sub-optimal performance across most tip-speed ratios.
For the two-bladed turbine, the optimal tip-speed ratio decreased slightly from 2.15 for the negative camber to 1.98 for the positive camber.
The negatively cambered blades reduced the peak loading by 13% compared to the symmetrical blades.
The validated numerical simulations suggested that a small but positive total camber (geometric plus virtual) is optimal for this turbine configuration.
The virtual camber estimation method has higher uncertainty for the downstream portion of the rotation due to the effects of induction.
Particle image velocimetry was used to explore the in-rotor flow evolution through the cycle for the different blade configurations.
The study found that the influence of geometric camber is non-linear, and that a simplistic summation of geometric and virtual camber may be overly simplistic.
The experimental performance measurements were compared across a range of tip-speed ratios up to 3.5.
